item.title: Suki Waterhouse on Feeling ‘Wiser & Also Sillier Than Ever’ on ‘Loveland’ Album, How Opening for Taylor Swift’s Eras Tour Will Impact Her Next Trek
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to the Billboard Pop Shop Podcast. Today, we're talking to singer and actress Suki Waterhouse about her brand new album, Loveland. Suki, congrats on the release!
[Soft music transitions in]
Host: Suki, your last album, Memoir of a Sparklemuffin, came out in September 2024, and now you're back with Loveland. What inspired this new record?
Suki Waterhouse: Well, I had my daughter in March 2024, and I started working on this album just a couple of weeks after she was born. It's been a huge shift for me, becoming a mother, and this record is all about that journey.
Host: That's amazing. You co-wrote every track on the project with some incredible songwriters and producers, including Amy Allen and Aaron Dessner. What was that experience like?
Suki Waterhouse: It was incredible. I connect with people quickly, and once I'm in the room, I open up and we can get down to business. We had some amazing conversations and created some really special songs.
Host: One of those songs is "Back in Love," the lead single from the album. What made you choose that as the first release?
Suki Waterhouse: It was the last song I wrote for the album, and it felt like healing. It made me excited to go back out on the road and perform. It's a song that makes me dream big.
Host: That's great. And finally, we have to talk about the Britpop influence on the album. Can you tell us a bit about that?
Suki Waterhouse: [laughs] Well, I think it's just a part of who I am as a British person. It's in my blood, and it bleeds into my music.
[Outro music plays]
Host: Thanks for chatting with us, Suki. Loveland is out now, so be sure to check it out.
[Outro music continues to play until the end]
